name: Chad
summary: A former French colony in the Sahel, independent in 1960; long civil wars and a war with Libya (1978–87).

knownFor.label: Lake Chad
knownFor.note: A lake that has shrunk greatly since the 1960s.

terrain.value: The Sahara in the north, the Sahelian belt in the centre and Sudanic savanna in the south.

climate.value: A largely desert climate in the north.

resources.value: Oil (production began in 2003), cotton and livestock.

disasters.value: Droughts and the shrinking of Lake Chad.

urbanisation.value: N'Djamena is the capital and largest city.

disease.value: Malnutrition; 2024 Global Hunger Index score of 36.4 (125th of 127).

migration.value: About 1.3 million Sudanese refugees were hosted in 2025.

economicBase.value: Oil, cotton and herding, with most people living by farming or livestock.

tradeRoutes.value: The Chad–Cameroon pipeline links the southern oilfields to Cameroon's Atlantic coast.

wealth.value: One of the world's least developed countries (HDI 0.416 in 2023; 190th).

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A presidential republic with strong military influence.

keyRulers.value: François Tombalbaye (first president, 1960). Hissène Habré (took the capital in 1979). Idriss Déby (from 1990). Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Coups and rebellions are recurrent; in 2021 a military council named the late president’s son interim president.

institutions.value: Weak; listed as a failed state by the Fund for Peace, and corruption is described as rife.

stability.value: Civil wars from 1965 to 1979 and from 2005 to 2010.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: An experienced army, which has fought rebels and jihadist groups in the Sahel.

territoryChange.value: Won the Aouzou Strip back from Libya (1994).

alliancesRivals.value: The last French soldiers left in early 2025.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: Literacy of 33%, among the lowest in Sub-Saharan Africa.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Roads, with many seasonal tracks, and Lake Chad boats.

religion.value: Muslims mainly in the north and east; Christians and animists mainly in the south.

languageWriting.value: French and Arabic are the official languages.

artsArchitecture.value: Rock art in the Ennedi and Tibesti mountains, and the Ennedi Plateau World Heritage Site.

socialStructure.value: Over 200 ethnic groups, divided between a mainly Muslim north and a Christian and animist south.

sharedIdentity.value: A north–south divide, with French and Arabic as official languages.

dailyLife.value: Families live in mud houses or tents and eat millet porridge.

neighbours.value: Libya, Sudan, Central African Republic, Cameroon, Nigeria, Niger.

ideasReligions.value: Islam is the largest religion, followed by Christianity.

colonisation.value: A French colony from the early 1900s to 1960.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Chad continues as an independent state.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
